context_label: Unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) after imatinib and sunitinib

purpose: Regorafenib aims to control gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) after progression on, or intolerance to, both imatinib and sunitinib. Your team explains the likely benefit, uncertainty, alternatives and the monitoring needed for your circumstances.
schedule_summary: National Cancer Control Programme 00244 uses regorafenib 160 mg by mouth once daily on days 1–21 of a 28-day cycle, followed by 7 days off. The team may reduce the dose in 40 mg steps or interrupt treatment; do not change the dose or restart independently.

agents.name: Regorafenib
agents.type: Oral targeted therapy: tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.mechanism: Blocks several growth and blood-vessel signals
agents.explanation: Regorafenib inhibits several kinases that help tumour cells grow and blood vessels support them. In gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) it is used after imatinib and sunitinib. Effects on healthy tissues make skin care, blood-pressure checks and early liver monitoring particularly important.
agents.watch: Report sore hands or feet early. Seek urgent help for yellow eyes, dark urine, severe abdominal pain, significant bleeding, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache or confusion.
risks: Hand-foot skin reaction, rash, mouth soreness, fatigue and reduced appetite
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, dehydration and weight loss
High blood pressure and changes in thyroid function
Liver injury, sometimes severe or fatal; frequent early blood tests are essential
Infection, anaemia, low platelets and bleeding; rare heart ischaemia, bowel perforation or abnormal bowel connections (fistulas)
Impaired wound healing and pregnancy harm
Rare severe skin reactions, artery-wall bulging or tearing, small-vessel clotting with kidney injury, or brain effects causing confusion, seizures or visual changes

anatomy: Severe headache, confusion, seizures or new visual problems can signal serious blood-pressure or brain effects. Seek urgent help.
Soreness and taste change can reduce intake. Use gentle mouth care and ask for symptom support early.
Attend blood-pressure checks. Chest pain, new breathlessness, fainting or severe palpitations needs urgent assessment.
Liver injury can occur without early symptoms. Keep blood-test appointments and report yellow eyes or dark urine.
Report reduced urine, swelling or dehydration. Your team checks kidney function and may check urine protein when indicated.
Report fever, sudden illness, unusual bruising or bleeding. Heavy bleeding, black stools or coughing blood needs urgent help.
Ask early about diarrhoea. Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or inability to drink requires urgent advice.
Report soreness, redness, cracks or blisters early. Reduce rubbing and heat and follow the skin-care plan.

monitoring_test_details.label: Liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect potentially serious liver injury before symptoms develop.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before treatment, at least every 2 weeks for the first 2 months, then at least monthly or more often when indicated.

monitoring_test_details.label: Blood pressure
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect and manage high blood pressure.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline, weekly for the first 6 weeks, then before each cycle and as indicated.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count and kidney tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check bleeding/infection risk, hydration and kidney function.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and regularly during treatment; the team specifies the sampling dates and extra tests for symptoms or previous abnormalities.

monitoring_test_details.label: Thyroid function
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify thyroid abnormalities that may need treatment.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and subsequently when clinically indicated.

monitoring_test_details.label: Pancreatic enzymes
monitoring_test_details.timing: Lipase or amylase when clinically indicated; these are not universal fixed-interval tumour-marker tests.

monitoring_test_details.label: Heart rhythm and electrolytes
monitoring_test_details.timing: electrocardiogram (heart tracing) and relevant electrolyte review when risk factors, interacting medicines or symptoms indicate them.

monitoring_test_details.label: Warfarin clotting test
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check anticoagulation when regorafenib is combined with warfarin.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Monitor international normalised ratio (warfarin clotting test) closely if taking warfarin; the team specifies the testing and dose plan.

monitoring_test_details.label: Hands, feet, mouth and healing
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect painful skin effects, mouth injury or wound problems.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Check before treatment and review symptoms during each cycle; report soreness early and coordinate any planned operation.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour response review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess benefit separately from treatment-safety tests.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Your gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) specialist sets imaging and clinical-review timing. This advanced-disease plan assesses tumour control, symptoms and whether treatment remains useful.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Confirm that both prior imatinib and sunitinib treatments have been reviewed. Reconcile all prescription, non-prescription and herbal products, including warfarin and the liver enzyme cytochrome P450 3A4 interactions; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Agree liver-test and blood-pressure appointments before starting. No routine separate premedication is specified; oral emetogenic potential is minimal-to-low. Start the agreed hand-foot skin-care measures and report painful areas early. Use prescribed diarrhoea, nausea, blood-pressure or thyroid treatment. Tell the team before surgery or dental procedures because healing may be affected.

support.title: Oral medicine handling
support.text: Keep tablets or capsules in their supplied packaging, away from children, and follow the pharmacy storage instructions. Do not share medicines or alter the dose yourself. Ask the pharmacy before crushing, opening or dispersing a medicine; formulation-specific instructions differ. Return unused treatment to the pharmacy.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility, effective contraception, pregnancy prevention and breastfeeding before treatment. Your team must give the product-specific precautions and duration for you and your partner. Tell oncology promptly about a possible pregnancy.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) is a distinct tumour type. A specialist team reviews pathology, KIT/platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha and other relevant molecular findings, prior treatment, symptoms and scans. Surgery may be appropriate for resectable disease or selected situations. Radiotherapy has a selective role, rather than being a routine partner to these tablets. Nutrition, symptom control and supportive or palliative care can be used alongside active cancer treatment.

support.title: Missed or vomited doses
support.text: Take a missed dose when remembered on the same day. Do not take two doses on one day. Do not take extra tablets after vomiting; contact the team if vomiting continues.

evidence.title: GRID: regorafenib after imatinib and sunitinib in advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST)
evidence.summary: GRID compared regorafenib plus best supportive care with placebo plus best supportive care in advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) after imatinib and sunitinib. Regorafenib improved progression-free survival. This explains its later-line disease-control role.
evidence.intro: GRID compared regorafenib plus best supportive care with placebo plus best supportive care in advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) after imatinib and sunitinib. Regorafenib improved progression-free survival. This explains its later-line disease-control role.
evidence.caveat: Progression-free survival is not the same as a proven overall-survival gain or an individual prognosis. Crossover complicates overall-survival interpretation. Do not use colorectal CORRECT or liver-cancer RESORCE results as gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) estimates.

questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: Regorafenib aims to control gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) after progression on, or intolerance to, both imatinib and sunitinib. Your team explains the likely benefit, uncertainty, alternatives and the monitoring needed for your circumstances. GIST is a distinct tumour type. A specialist team reviews pathology, KIT/platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha and other relevant molecular findings, prior treatment, symptoms and scans. Surgery may be appropriate for resectable disease or selected situations. Radiotherapy has a selective role, rather than being a routine partner to these tablets. Nutrition, symptom control and supportive or palliative care can be used alongside active cancer treatment.

National Cancer Control Programme 00244 uses regorafenib 160 mg by mouth once daily on days 1–21 of a 28-day cycle, followed by 7 days off. The team may reduce the dose in 40 mg steps or interrupt treatment; do not change the dose or restart independently.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: What should I do about a missed or vomited dose?
questions.a: Take a missed dose when remembered on the same day. Do not take two doses on one day. Do not take extra tablets after vomiting; contact the team if vomiting continues.

questions.q: Can I take other medicines or supplements?
questions.a: Confirm that both prior imatinib and sunitinib treatments have been reviewed. Reconcile all prescription, non-prescription and herbal products, including warfarin and the liver enzyme cytochrome P450 3A4 interactions; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Agree liver-test and blood-pressure appointments before starting.

questions.q: Why do I need checks if I feel well?
questions.a: High blood pressure, thyroid changes, liver injury or low blood counts may be detected before you notice symptoms. The required checks differ by medicine; keep your individual schedule.
